question: Two players bet on a fair coin tossed every second for a year. How long is the luckier one usually ahead?
answer: Most of the year. In half of games the leader is ahead for more than 311 days; in one game in 20, for all but about 14 hours. Erasing a lead takes an equal run the other way, and such runs are slow, so one player often stays in front for months on end.
move: A long lead in a fair game is evidence of nothing but time.
reference: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Volume 1, 3rd edition, Wiley, 1968
